# client-routing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** React Router data-router guide (loaders, error boundaries) — https://micropyramid.com/blog/react-router-for-navigation/ ; inherited Web Craft Pro Max rules R-5.2-3, R-10.1-4 and cure CD-06, mapped in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md
- **Depends on:** frontend-core, data-fetching
- **Feeds into:** ui-states, frontend-state

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building or changing the route structure of a single-page app or hybrid site — defining routes, navigation, guards, deep links, or the 404 view.
- **Do NOT use when:** the site is a set of plain server-rendered pages with no client router (the server framework's routing and frontend-core apply), or the question is what data a route loads (data-fetching owns fetching; this skill owns the URL and navigation contract).

## Rules

1. **FE-221 — Every meaningful view has a real URL.** If a user would bookmark it, share it, or return to it, it is a route — not a component swapped by local state.
2. **FE-222 — No state-flag navigation.** Refresh, deep link, and the back/forward buttons must all land on the correct view. A view reachable only by clicking from another view is a defect.
3. **FE-223 — Loaders fetch before render, errors stay local.** Routes load their data in route loaders (or the framework equivalent) and each route carries an error boundary, so a failed route renders its error view inside the layout instead of crashing the app shell.
4. **FE-224 — Unknown paths render the designed 404.** A catch-all route shows the product's 404 view with a path back into the product (inherited cure CD-06: design the 404 and error pages). A blank screen on a bad URL is a defect.
5. **FE-225 — Guards are UX only.** A route guard may redirect an unauthenticated user to login, but protected data is authorized by the API on every request, never by the router. Hiding a route is not protecting it.
6. **FE-226 — Crawlable links for indexable pages.** Navigation to public pages uses plain `<a href>` links to indexable canonical URLs — no JavaScript-only navigation for indexable pages (inherited R-5.2-3).
7. **FE-227 — One canonical URL per public page.** Every public page carries a canonical URL that returns 200 and does not redirect (inherited R-10.1-4; gate G-SCH-02).
8. **FE-228 — Navigation manages scroll and focus.** On navigation, scroll is restored on back/forward and reset on new views, and focus moves to the new view's heading or main region so keyboard and screen-reader users start at the top of the new content, not stranded mid-page.
9. **FE-229 — No full-page reloads inside the SPA.** In-app navigation uses the router's link component; a full document reload between app views breaks FE-222's back/forward and scroll contract.
10. **FE-230 — Route changes are announced.** The document title updates on every route change, and route transitions expose the loading state owned by ui-states — a silent, frozen screen during navigation is a missing state, not a fast load.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-111 — State-flag navigation.** Banned: switching views with a state variable (`const [page, setPage] = useState('home')`) instead of routes. Defeats: DET-UX-014. Instead: define a route per view and navigate with the router. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-112 — Blank screen on an unknown URL.** Banned: a route table with no catch-all, so an unmatched path renders an empty shell. Defeats: DET-UX-010 (see also DET-VIS-032). Instead: a catch-all route rendering the designed 404 view (FE-224). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-113 — JavaScript-only navigation for indexable pages.** Banned: `<div onClick>` or button handlers as the only way to reach a public page. Defeats: DET-UX-002. Instead: real anchor links to canonical URLs (inherited R-5.2-3). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-114 — Router guard as the authorization boundary.** Banned: treating a client-side guard as protection for data the API serves without its own check. Defeats: DET-FAKE-002 (see also DET-VIS-032). Instead: the guard redirects for UX; the API authorizes every request (FE-225). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-FE-111 — Cold-load and traversal pass.** Verifies: FE-221, FE-222, FE-224. Check: automated — Playwright: cold-load a nested route directly in a fresh tab and assert the correct view renders; traverse five views using link navigation plus back/forward and assert each lands correctly; load a nonsense URL and assert the designed 404 view appears. Pass: all assertions green. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-112 — Refresh sweep.** Verifies: FE-222. Check: manual — refresh the browser on every route in the route table during QA; each must return the same view with its data. Pass: every route survives refresh. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-113 — Authorization boundary probe.** Verifies: FE-225. Check: automated — request each guarded route's API endpoints with no credentials and with a non-privileged session (e.g. `curl -i https://<host>/api/admin/users`); assert 401/403 and no protected payload in any response. Pass: no endpoint leaks data. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-114 — Focus and scroll check.** Verifies: FE-228, FE-230. Check: manual browser verification — navigate by keyboard through three views; after each navigation, focus sits on the new view's heading/main region, the title has changed, and back returns the previous scroll position. Pass: all three behaviors observed. Fail: warn, fix before release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- If a user would bookmark it, it is a route.
- Refresh, deep link, back button — all three must land correctly.
- Guards redirect; APIs authorize.
- Unknown path = designed 404, never a blank screen.
- Navigation moves focus and updates the title.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every meaningful view has its own route and URL (FE-221).
- [ ] Playwright cold-load/traversal/404 pass is green (G-FE-111).
- [ ] Refresh sweep done on every route (G-FE-112).
- [ ] API probe confirms no guarded data leaks (G-FE-113).
- [ ] Public navigation uses real anchor links to canonical URLs (FE-226, FE-227).
- [ ] Focus, title, and scroll behavior verified by keyboard (G-FE-114).

# component-library

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Structuring your Storybook (component-driven development, stories per variant and state) — https://storybook.js.org/blog/structuring-your-storybook/ ; GOV.UK Design System, button component — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/
- **Depends on:** design-tokens, design-system
- **Feeds into:** frontend-core, layout-responsive, forms, ui-states

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building, extending, or reviewing the components pages are assembled from — their variants, state sets, iconography, and content stress behavior. WCPM's component bans and the CMP and ICO families land here, as does the component half of WCPM §8 (components & states).
- **Do NOT use when:** the state belongs to a data view rather than a component (ui-states owns the view-level state matrix), or the question is page composition (layout-responsive, design-system). Components are built here; pages are composed elsewhere.

## Rules

1. **FE-061 — Built bottom-up, in the workshop.** Components are built and reviewed in Storybook, isolated from pages, one story per variant and per state. A component first seen inside a finished page was never reviewed.
2. **FE-062 — The full state set, or a written exception.** Every component ships its applicable states — default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error — or its state matrix states explicitly why a state does not apply (DET-VIS-032).
3. **FE-063 — Behavior lives in the component.** Focus order, keyboard interaction, disabled semantics, and ARIA wiring are implemented and tested once, inside the component — never re-implemented per page.
4. **FE-064 — One icon set.** One icon library or custom set, one stroke weight, one metaphor style across the whole library (DET-VIS-025). A second set is a system change (FE-024), not a per-component choice.
5. **FE-065 — Emoji are never structural icons.** Icons in headings, feature lists, and navigation are drawn icons from the set. Emoji may appear in informal copy, never as the icon for a feature (DET-VIS-016).
6. **FE-066 — Stress-tested with real content.** Components are tested with the longest real names, labels, and words the product will hold; overflow, clipping, or broken wrapping at ordinary content lengths is a component bug (DET-VIS-007).
7. **FE-067 — Variants express hierarchy.** Button and action variants differ by emphasis and context (primary / secondary / destructive / text; sizes by placement), not one treatment at one size for every action (DET-VIS-031). Destructive actions are never styled as primary.
8. **FE-068 — Badges carry actionable information.** A badge or pill states something the user can act on — a status, a genuine novelty, a filterable category. Decorative labeling is removed (DET-VIS-033).
9. **FE-069 — Cards earn their weight.** In a grid, content of unequal importance gets unequal weight: one item may be featured, span wider, or carry richer media. Identical cards are permitted only where the content is genuinely parallel — and their copy must still be specific, not interchangeable (DET-VIS-003).
10. **FE-070 — Pages assemble, they do not imitate.** A page needing something new extends the library; hand-rolled markup that duplicates a library component is a defect, found by the grep gate (G-FE-033), not by taste.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-031 — The interchangeable card grid.** Banned: a grid of identical cards whose descriptions could be swapped between cards — or between products — without anyone noticing. Defeats: DET-VIS-003. Instead: cards weighted by importance (FE-069) with copy that names this product's specific capability. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-032 — The icon-in-tinted-circle formula.** Banned: every feature icon presented in an identical soft-tinted circle or rounded square in the accent color, in every grid on the site. Defeats: DET-VIS-026. Instead: icon treatment that varies by context or uses a distinctive brand device; the chip is one option, not the universal default. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-033 — Emoji as feature icons.** Banned: 🚀 ⚡ 🔒-style emoji prefixed to feature headings or list items in place of an icon system. Defeats: DET-VIS-016. Instead: drawn icons from the library's single set (FE-064). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-034 — One button for everything.** Banned: a single button size, radius, and treatment for every action on the site, primary and secondary differing only by fill. Defeats: DET-VIS-031. Instead: a variant hierarchy by emphasis and context, with destructive actions distinctly styled and never primary (FE-067). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-035 — The template pricing table.** Banned: the three-tier, middle-highlighted, check-icon pricing table applied to a product whose model is not seat-based SaaS. Defeats: DET-VIS-036. Instead: pricing presentation that follows the actual model — usage bands, a calculator, one-time pricing (pricing rules owned by D1's pricing-monetization). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-031 — Storybook visual regression.** Verifies: FE-061, FE-062, FE-066. Check: automated — Storybook test-runner plus screenshot visual regression over all stories runs in CI, including the long-content stress stories. Pass: all tests green, zero unreviewed screenshot diffs. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-032 — State matrix coverage.** Verifies: FE-062, FE-063. Check: manual — walk the state matrix per component: every applicable state (default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error) has a story, and every non-applicable state has its written reason. Pass: matrix complete. Fail: warn and hold the component. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-033 — Duplicate-markup grep.** Verifies: FE-070. Check: automated — grep page code for raw `<button`/`<input`/`<select` markup duplicating a library component, and for icon imports outside the library's single set (FE-064). Pass: zero hits. Fail: block until the page uses the library. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-034 — Icon and badge audit.** Verifies: FE-064, FE-065, FE-068. Check: manual + automated — scan headings and feature lists for emoji codepoints (automated); screenshot all icons in one view to check stroke weight and metaphor consistency; count badges per viewport and name the action each enables. Pass: no structural emoji, one icon style, every badge actionable. Fail: warn; block if emoji carry a feature list. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One story per variant and state, or it wasn't reviewed.
- Behavior is built once, inside the component.
- One icon set, one stroke weight; emoji are not icons.
- Test with the longest real content, not the placeholder.
- Pages assemble from the library — they never imitate it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every variant and state has a Storybook story (G-FE-031).
- [ ] State matrix complete, with written reasons for non-applicable states (G-FE-032).
- [ ] Longest real content renders without overflow or clipping (FE-066).
- [ ] All icons come from the single set at one stroke weight (FE-064).
- [ ] No emoji serve as structural icons anywhere (FE-065).
- [ ] No raw component-duplicating markup in page code (G-FE-033).
- [ ] Every badge names an action the user can take (FE-068).
- [ ] Button variants express hierarchy; destructive is never primary (FE-067).

# data-fetching

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** TanStack Query, Important Defaults — https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults
- **Depends on:** frontend-state, ui-states
- **Feeds into:** frontend-core, data-visualisation, pwa-offline

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** reading or mutating server data from the client; setting up a query cache; fixing duplicate requests, stale renders, race conditions, or fetches scattered through components.
- **Do NOT use when:** the state never leaves the client — that is frontend-state. Do not use this skill to design the API itself (endpoints, payloads, status codes); that is D2/D4's architecture and backend work — this skill governs how the client consumes it.

## Rules

1. **FE-201 — All server reads go through the query layer.** Reads use the dedicated query cache (TanStack Query, or framework loaders/actions in Next.js/Nuxt-style stacks). Fetch-on-mount `useEffect` sprawl across components is forbidden.
2. **FE-202 — Query keys mirror the API.** Keys follow a stable scheme that names the resource and its parameters (`['orders', { status }]`, `['orders', id]`), so caching, deduplication, and invalidation behave predictably.
3. **FE-203 — Freshness is a decision per data type.** `staleTime` is set deliberately for each query based on how fast its data changes; accepting a global default without considering the data is not a decision.
4. **FE-204 — Stale responses cannot win.** Requests are keyed or cancellable so that fast navigation or changing parameters cannot let an older, slower response overwrite a newer view.
5. **FE-205 — Every outcome lands in the state matrix.** Each query's loading and error outcomes render through the view's ui-states matrix; errors are never swallowed silently and never leave a blank region.
6. **FE-206 — Retries come from the query layer.** Failed queries retry with the layer's backoff defaults; hand-rolled retry loops in components are forbidden.
7. **FE-207 — Mutations update exactly what they affect.** A mutation invalidates or optimistically updates precisely the affected queries. Optimistic updates always carry a rollback path that runs on failure.
8. **FE-208 — Production renders real server data only.** No fixture, canned, or hard-coded response stands in for a live endpoint in a production path; demo data is labeled as demo wherever it legitimately appears (WCPM DAT family, docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md §2.4).
9. **FE-209 — One in-flight request per key.** The same endpoint is never fetched repeatedly for one page render; shared data is requested once and served to all consumers from the cache.
10. **FE-210 — Offline behavior is designed.** Losing connectivity mid-session produces the designed error state, and reconnecting recovers through the query layer's refetch — not a manual reload (with ui-states).
11. **FE-211 — Inherited fetching law.** The WCPM §9 engineering rules apply as cited in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md §2.2, and fetching work is designed to pass the G-ENG gate family.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-101 — Canned responses as live data.** Banned: shipping fixture or hard-coded responses presented as live server data. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: query the real endpoint through the query layer; if the endpoint does not exist yet, the feature does not ship (FE-208). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-102 — Unkeyed requests racing.** Banned: issuing requests whose responses can arrive out of order and overwrite the current view. Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: key the query by its parameters so only the current key's data renders (FE-204). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-103 — Swallowed errors.** Banned: empty `catch` blocks, silent fallbacks, or error paths that render nothing. Defeats: DET-VIS-032. Instead: the error outcome renders the view's designed error state with a retry (FE-205). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-104 — Optimistic update with no rollback.** Banned: applying an optimistic change that stays on screen when the mutation fails. Defeats: DET-FAKE-011. Instead: snapshot the affected queries, roll back on error, and show the error state (FE-207). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-105 — Fixture filtering sold as search.** Banned: filtering or sorting a local fixture client-side while presenting it as server search over the real dataset. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: send the query to the server and render its results, with the result count from the server (FE-208). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-FE-101 — Network-count cache test.** Verifies: FE-201, FE-203, FE-209. Check: automated — Playwright navigates view A → B → A while counting requests; the shared endpoint is requested once, then served from cache with background revalidation per its `staleTime`. Pass: exactly one network request for the shared endpoint across the sequence. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-102 — Race test.** Verifies: FE-204. Check: automated — a test delays the first of two parameter changes so its response arrives after the second's, then asserts the view renders the second (current) key's data. Pass: the final render matches the current parameters. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-103 — Offline drill.** Verifies: FE-205, FE-210. Check: manual — go offline mid-session on the main views; confirm the designed error state appears, then reconnect and confirm recovery without a manual reload. Pass: error state and recovery both behave as designed. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-104 — Rollback test.** Verifies: FE-207. Check: automated — a test forces a mutation to fail after its optimistic update and asserts the UI reverts to the pre-mutation data and shows the error state. Pass: full rollback with a visible error. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Server state lives in the query cache, nowhere else.
- Keys mirror the API; freshness is chosen per data type.
- A stale response never overwrites a newer view.
- Optimistic always rolls back.
- Errors render a state; they are never swallowed.

## Checklist

- [ ] All server reads go through the query layer; no fetch-on-mount sprawl (FE-201).
- [ ] Query keys follow the resource scheme; `staleTime` is set per data type (FE-202, FE-203).
- [ ] Network-count test: shared endpoint requested once across A → B → A (G-FE-101).
- [ ] Race test: the current key's data is what renders (G-FE-102).
- [ ] Offline drill: designed error state appears and recovers on reconnect (G-FE-103).
- [ ] Failed mutations roll back their optimistic updates (G-FE-104).
- [ ] No fixture or canned response stands in for a live endpoint (BAN-FE-101).

# data-visualisation

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Datawrapper, A friendly guide to choosing a chart type — https://www.datawrapper.de/blog/chart-types-guide ; inherited Web Craft Pro Max §6.7 data-visualization rules, cure CD-17, parameter DAT-07, and BAN-099/BAN-120, mapped in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md
- **Depends on:** frontend-core, design-tokens
- **Feeds into:** component-library, ui-states

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** any chart, graph, stat band, or data graphic is being designed or rendered — dashboards, reports, marketing pages, admin panels.
- **Do NOT use when:** the data itself is being collected or computed (D5/D12 own data and metrics definitions), or the "chart" is a single number with no comparison — that is copy, and frontend-core plus the fact-sheet rules govern it.

## Rules

1. **FE-261 — Message first, chart second.** Before choosing a library or chart type, write the one-sentence statement the chart must make (change over time, comparison, share, correlation, flow, geography). If the sentence cannot be stated, the chart is decoration and is removed.
2. **FE-262 — Type matches the message.** Lines for change over time, bars for comparison across categories, scatter for correlation, stacked bars for part-to-whole, histograms for distribution (inherited §6.7). A type chosen because it "looks good" fails this rule.
3. **FE-263 — Bar axes start at zero.** A truncated bar axis is a defect unless the truncation is explicitly justified in the project notes and flagged on the chart itself.
4. **FE-264 — No 3D charts, no overloaded pies, no implied correlation.** No 3D chart effects; no pie with more than 5 slices (use a stacked bar or bar chart instead); no dual axes implying a correlation without a stated basis.
5. **FE-265 — Color encodes meaning, and never alone.** One accent color carries the story, gray carries context. Series colors are checked for colorblind distinguishability, rainbow palettes are forbidden, and meaning is never carried by color alone — series are labeled or patterned as well (inherited §6.7).
6. **FE-266 — Every chart is labeled and sourced.** Axis labels, units, and the data source with its date appear on or directly under every chart (inherited cure CD-17; parameter DAT-07). An unsourced chart is treated like an unsourced statistic and escalates per DET-VIS-035.
7. **FE-267 — The title states the conclusion.** A chart's title says what the data shows ("Signups doubled after the March launch"), not what it contains ("Signups"). Series are labeled directly where possible instead of forcing legend lookups.
8. **FE-268 — Every chart ships an accessible alternative.** Each chart is accompanied by its data table or a text summary (visually hidden is acceptable) describing the series and the takeaway, reachable via `aria-describedby` or adjacent markup.
9. **FE-269 — Real data only.** Charts render real, possible values that add up. Demo or sample data is plausible, specific, and uneven — and clearly marked as sample wherever it appears (inherited BAN-099).
10. **FE-270 — Uncertainty is shown, not hidden.** Where the underlying data carries ranges, estimates, or partial coverage, the chart shows it (range bands, "estimated" markers, a coverage note) instead of drawing a single confident line.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-131 — The unsourced or impossible chart.** Banned: a chart with no source line, no axis labels, or values that cannot be true (shares summing past 100%, counts below zero). Defeats: DET-VIS-035. Instead: labeled axes, units, source with date, and real values (FE-266, FE-269). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-132 — The truncated bar axis.** Banned: a bar chart whose value axis starts above zero to exaggerate a small difference. Defeats: DET-VIS-035. Instead: start the axis at zero (FE-263); if scale genuinely hides the story, switch to a dot plot and say why. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-133 — Decoration wearing a chart's clothes.** Banned: 3D bars, exploded pies, and gradient-filled shapes whose form distorts or hides the values. Defeats: DET-VIS-028. Instead: a flat stacked bar or bar chart with direct labels (FE-262, FE-264). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-134 — Rainbow, color-only encoding.** Banned: a rainbow or random multi-hue palette where hue is the only thing distinguishing series. Defeats: DET-VIS-022. Instead: one accent plus gray context, direct labels, colorblind-checked pairs (FE-265). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-131 — Accessible-alternative DOM check.** Verifies: FE-268. Check: automated — script/DOM query over the built pages: every chart root (`canvas`, `svg` with a chart role) must have an accompanying data table in the DOM or an `aria-describedby` target containing a text summary. Pass: 0 chart roots without an alternative. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-132 — Message test.** Verifies: FE-261, FE-262, FE-267. Check: manual — for each chart, state its one-sentence message from the title alone, then confirm the chart type is the family that answers that message per FE-262. Pass: every chart's type matches its stated message. Fail: warn, rework before release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-133 — Axis, label, and source inspection.** Verifies: FE-263, FE-266, FE-269. Check: manual — inspect each rendered chart: bar axes start at zero (or carry the on-chart truncation flag), axes and units are labeled, the source and date are present, and values are possible and sum correctly. Pass: all charts pass all four checks. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-134 — Colorblind simulation pass.** Verifies: FE-265. Check: manual with tooling — view each chart through a colorblind simulator (browser DevTools vision-deficiency emulation) and in grayscale; every series must remain distinguishable by label, position, or pattern. Pass: no series becomes ambiguous. Fail: warn, fix before release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No message, no chart.
- Bars start at zero; pies stop at five slices.
- Every chart: labels, units, source, date.
- Color means something — and is never the only signal.
- If it can't be read as a table, it isn't accessible.

## Checklist

- [ ] Each chart's one-sentence message is written down and its type matches it (FE-261, FE-262).
- [ ] Bar axes start at zero or carry the on-chart truncation flag (FE-263).
- [ ] No 3D charts, no pies over 5 slices, no unstated dual axes (FE-264).
- [ ] DOM check passes: every chart has a table or text alternative (G-FE-131).
- [ ] Axis/source inspection passes on every chart (G-FE-133).
- [ ] Colorblind and grayscale pass done; series labeled directly (G-FE-134, FE-265).
- [ ] Sample data, where used, is marked as sample (FE-269).

# design-system

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** GOV.UK Design System, button component (usage guidance incl. when not to use) — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/ ; Design Tokens Specification 2025.10, first stable version announcement — https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2025/10/28/design-tokens-specification-reaches-first-stable-version/
- **Depends on:** design-tokens
- **Feeds into:** frontend-core, component-library, typography, layout-responsive

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** establishing or governing the system itself — its tokens, component inventory, usage rules, and changelog — and when reviewing a page for system-level failures: monotony, drift, invented proof. This skill is the primary home for WCPM's visual-language material: §2 catalog (as reference), §3 diagnosis and CV cures, §4 design brief and distinctiveness, and §6 visual craft.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is a single token value (design-tokens), a single component's internals (component-library), or a single page's layout (layout-responsive). The system governs; those skills execute.

## Rules

1. **FE-021 — The system is four artifacts.** The token set, the component library, written usage rules, and a changelog. A visual decision that exists only inside one page's code is not part of the system and does not ship as one.
2. **FE-022 — Every decision traces.** Each visual choice on a shipped page traces to a token, a library component, or a documented one-off exception with a written reason. Untraceable styling is drift and is removed or absorbed into the system.
3. **FE-023 — Guidance includes refusal.** Every component's documentation states its purpose, its variants, and at least one "do not use when" case, on the GOV.UK pattern. A component documented only with happy paths will be misused.
4. **FE-024 — Changes are versioned.** A token or component change ships with a changelog entry and a visual-regression pass, never as a silent edit. Consumers of the system learn about change from the changelog, not from a screenshot diff.
5. **FE-025 — Composition varies by role.** Section composition follows content role (hero, proof, dense content, closing): a page where every section shares the same padding, alignment, and loudest element fails system review (DET-VIS-001, DET-VIS-002, DET-VIS-010).
6. **FE-026 — Proof may outrank headings.** Hierarchy serves the message: a metric, a product shot, or a customer quote may be the most prominent element in its section. The heading is not entitled to be loudest by default.
7. **FE-027 — Diagnose before redesigning.** Visual failures are diagnosed against the parameter catalog (WCPM §2, served in this repo by DET-VIS-001…044) and cured with the matching cure rules (CV family) — not by restyling on taste. Clusters are scored as clusters: 3 or more minor tells in one component or section count as one major (WCPM CLU-01…06; enforced by G-DES-02).
8. **FE-028 — The acceptance bar is scored, not felt.** A page passes visual acceptance on the rubric: zero P0 parameters, rubric score ≥ 90, every category ≥ 7, zero F1–F8 auto-fails (WCPM G-DES-01). "Looks fine to me" is not a verdict — human detection of generated design is a near-chance instrument, so the score carries the decision.
9. **FE-029 — Distinctiveness is briefed before building.** Each project opens with a design brief that names its divergence: the visual choices that make this product unlike the template default (WCPM §4, BR- divergence rules and D-MIN minimum thresholds). A brief that could describe any SaaS site is rejected and rewritten.
10. **FE-030 — Imagery belongs to the system.** Photography and illustration follow one documented style and depict the business's real product, place, or people (DET-VIS-023); aspect ratios follow an art-directed grid so subjects survive their crops (DET-VIS-029). Stock or generated imagery depicting nothing real is not a system asset.
11. **FE-031 — The footer is designed.** The footer uses the system's tokens and carries a brand statement, real contact paths, and legal links that resolve — not a generic link grid pasted under the page (DET-VIS-009).

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-011 — The one-gradient, one-font "system".** Banned: calling a violet-blue gradient, one default font, and copy-pasted cards a design system. Defeats: DET-VIS-017. Instead: a chosen brand palette with roles, a deliberate type choice, and tokenized scales (design-tokens). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-012 — Invented social proof in the system.** Banned: logo clouds, testimonials, or metrics built from invented marks, people, or numbers as reusable system components. Defeats: DET-VIS-034. Instead: the component renders only real, permitted logos — and renders nothing when none exist. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-013 — Imagery that depicts nothing.** Banned: stock or AI imagery with no connection to the business as the system's default visual language. Defeats: DET-VIS-023. Instead: photographs of the actual bakery, its products, and its people, in one documented style. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-014 — The uniform section template.** Banned: one section layout — same padding, centered heading, three cards — repeated for every content role on a page. Defeats: DET-VIS-001. Instead: composition assigned per role (FE-025), with padding and alignment varying deliberately. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-015 — Generic wave and blob decoration.** Banned: SVG wave dividers, blurred color blobs, and dotted grids pasted between sections as decoration. Defeats: DET-VIS-028. Instead: transitions that are structural (color change, overlap, imagery) or a custom brand device used consistently. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-011 — DET-VIS cluster review.** Verifies: FE-025, FE-026, FE-027, FE-030, FE-031. Check: manual — per milestone, walk DET-VIS-001…044 in ID order against full-page screenshots at 1440px and 390px; mark each hit with a screenshot or measured value; apply the cluster rule (3+ minors in one section = 1 major). Pass: zero blockers, zero majors, clusters resolved. Fail: block the milestone. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-012 — Rubric acceptance score.** Verifies: FE-028. Check: manual scoring against the WCPM G-DES-01 bar — count P0 parameter hits, score the rubric, check every category ≥ 7 and zero F1–F8 auto-fails. Pass: 0 P0, score ≥ 90, all categories ≥ 7, zero auto-fails. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-013 — System trace audit.** Verifies: FE-021, FE-022, FE-024. Check: automated + manual — sample 10 styled elements per page and resolve each to a token, a library component, or a logged exception; confirm the system changelog has an entry for every token/component change in the release. Pass: 10 of 10 trace, changelog complete. Fail: block until drift is absorbed or removed. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-014 — Token and contrast enforcement.** Verifies: FE-022 (via design-tokens). Check: automated — the design-tokens gates run as this skill's enforcement arm: token-literal lint and the semantic-pair contrast script (G-FE-022, G-FE-023). Pass: both green. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Four artifacts: tokens, components, guidance, changelog.
- If it doesn't trace to the system, it's drift.
- Diagnose against parameters; never restyle on taste.
- The rubric decides — 0 P0, ≥ 90, no category under 7.
- Proof is allowed to be louder than the heading.

## Checklist

- [ ] The system has all four artifacts, current (FE-021).
- [ ] Sampled elements trace to token, component, or logged exception (G-FE-013).
- [ ] Every component documents a "do not use when" case (FE-023).
- [ ] Token/component changes carry changelog entries (FE-024).
- [ ] DET-VIS cluster review walked at 1440px and 390px (G-FE-011).
- [ ] Rubric acceptance bar met: 0 P0, ≥ 90, categories ≥ 7, zero F1–F8 (G-FE-012).
- [ ] Composition varies by section role; proof may outrank headings (FE-025, FE-026).
- [ ] Imagery depicts the real business in one documented style (FE-030).

# design-tokens

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10 (DTCG) — https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/ ; Style Dictionary, DTCG support — https://styledictionary.com/info/dtcg/
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: tokens are defined from the project's own visual decisions (user-supplied palette and type choices) in the token source files; this is the source layer, so nothing upstream feeds it. Its tokens feed design-system, component-library, typography, frontend-core, and motion.
- **Feeds into:** design-system, component-library, typography, frontend-core, motion

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** defining, changing, or auditing the token source files — the single place a visual value may be defined — and when a page shows value-level tells: gradient signatures, shadow monoculture, radius scatter, unchecked contrast. WCPM's colour/gradient bans (C- working IDs), the COL family, and the SPC family are prevented here, at the token layer.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is how a value is used (component-library, layout-responsive) or whether a composition works (design-system). Tokens define values; they do not design pages.

## Rules

1. **FE-041 — One format, one source.** Tokens are authored once in DTCG-format JSON — every token an object with `$value`, `$type`, and aliases by dot-path — and transformed by Style Dictionary (or Terrazzo) into CSS custom properties and other platform outputs. Hand-edited output files are defects.
2. **FE-042 — Three tiers.** Primitive (raw values) → semantic (roles: `color-action-primary`, `surface-raised`) → component. Theming happens at the semantic tier by overriding the same names; a theme never duplicates the primitive file.
3. **FE-043 — Semantic only in components.** Components reference semantic tokens exclusively. A primitive value, hex code, pixel, or millisecond literal in component styles is a defect found by lint, not by opinion.
4. **FE-044 — Every token is documented.** Each token carries a `$description` naming its role. Retired tokens are marked `$deprecated` with a pointer to their replacement — never silently deleted, so existing code fails loudly instead of drifting.
5. **FE-045 — Scales with named roles.** Elevation, radius, spacing, and duration are scales whose steps have roles (radius: input / card / pill; elevation: flat / card / menu / modal). Values are applied by role — the direct counter to the single-shadow default (DET-VIS-021) and radius scatter (DET-VIS-043).
6. **FE-046 — Pairs pass contrast before they are named.** A semantic foreground/background pair is only admitted to the token set after its WCAG ratio is computed: ≥ 4.5:1 for body text, ≥ 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators — including pairs that sit on tinted or gradient surfaces (DET-VIS-022).
7. **FE-047 — The palette has roles, not a hue.** The color system defines primary, secondary, semantic (success / warning / error), and a neutral ramp as distinct tokens. One accent hue covering every role, semantic states included, fails review (DET-VIS-020).
8. **FE-048 — Gradients are tokens with a reason, or absent.** A gradient exists only as a named token whose description states its brand basis and where it may be used. The violet-blue linear gradient is never a default primary, background, or text treatment (DET-VIS-017, DET-VIS-018).
9. **FE-049 — Dark surfaces are layered, not glowing.** Dark themes are built from layered surface tokens with restrained elevation; colored glow shadows are not an elevation device (DET-VIS-019).
10. **FE-050 — Token changes are reviewed as diffs.** Any change to the token source ships with a diff review and the design-system changelog entry (FE-024); a changed value with no diff review is treated as an accidental edit.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-021 — Raw values in component styles.** Banned: hex codes, pixel values, or millisecond literals written directly in component or page styles. Defeats: DET-VIS-020. Instead: `background: var(--color-action-primary); padding: var(--space-control-y) var(--space-control-x)`. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-022 — The violet-blue gradient as default.** Banned: a purple-to-blue (or purple-to-pink) linear gradient as the site's primary color event — hero background, buttons, or clipped into headline text. Defeats: DET-VIS-017. Instead: a chosen solid brand color with a supporting palette; a gradient only as a named token with a stated brand basis (FE-048). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-023 — Text on an unchecked surface.** Banned: naming a text/surface token pair that has never had its contrast ratio computed. Defeats: DET-VIS-022. Instead: darken the foreground token or deepen the surface until the pair computes ≥ 4.5:1, then admit the pair (FE-046). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-024 — One shadow for everything.** Banned: a single box-shadow value applied to cards, menus, modals, and buttons alike. Defeats: DET-VIS-021. Instead: the elevation scale — subtle for cards, deeper for menus and modals, matched to one light direction (FE-045). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-025 — Radius scatter.** Banned: unrelated border-radius values assigned per component with no role pattern. Defeats: DET-VIS-043. Instead: the radius scale applied by role (input / card / pill) everywhere (FE-045). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-021 — Token build in CI.** Verifies: FE-041, FE-042, FE-044. Check: automated — Style Dictionary build runs in CI; a broken alias, a missing `$type`, or a hand-edited output file fails the build. Pass: build green and outputs regenerate byte-identical from source. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-022 — Literal lint.** Verifies: FE-043. Check: automated — a stylelint custom rule (or grep script) fails on hex, px, or ms literals in component and page style files, excluding the token source and generated outputs. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block until values move into tokens. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-023 — Contrast script.** Verifies: FE-046, FE-047. Check: automated — a script computes the WCAG ratio for every semantic text-on-surface token pair, including tinted and gradient surfaces. Pass: every pair ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for pairs designated large-text or non-text). Fail: block; the pair is not admitted or is fixed. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-024 — Token diff review.** Verifies: FE-044, FE-050. Check: manual — review the token diff for the release: new tokens have descriptions, retired tokens are `$deprecated` with replacements, no scale gained a step without a role. Pass: diff approved and changelog entry present. Fail: warn and hold the token change. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Values live in tokens; components name roles, never numbers.
- Three tiers; themes override semantic names, not files.
- A pair passes contrast before it is named.
- Scales have roles — radius, elevation, spacing, duration.
- Retire with `$deprecated` and a pointer, never by deletion.

## Checklist

- [ ] Token source is DTCG JSON; outputs regenerate cleanly (G-FE-021).
- [ ] No raw hex/px/ms literals in component or page styles (G-FE-022).
- [ ] Every token carries a `$description` (FE-044).
- [ ] Every semantic text/surface pair computes ≥ 4.5:1 or ≥ 3:1 large (G-FE-023).
- [ ] Palette defines primary, secondary, semantic, and neutral roles (FE-047).
- [ ] Elevation and radius applied by role from their scales (FE-045).
- [ ] Any gradient is a named token with a stated brand basis (FE-048).
- [ ] Token diff reviewed; deprecations point at replacements (G-FE-024).

# forms

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** W3C WAI, Developing for Web Accessibility (labels, instructions, error help) — http://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/developing/ ; NN/g, Empty-State Interface Design (form-adjacent state copy) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/ ; inherited Web Craft Pro Max rules R-11.4-1…R-11.4-5, mapped in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md
- **Depends on:** component-library, ui-states
- **Feeds into:** frontend-core, data-fetching

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building or reviewing any form — signup, checkout, settings, search-with-filters, multi-step flows — its labels, validation, error handling, and submission behavior.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is server-side validation rules or persistence (D4 owns those; this skill owns what the user sees and how the form behaves), or the surface is a single button with no input (component-library covers it).

## Rules

1. **FE-241 — Every control has a visible, associated label.** Each input carries a `<label>` tied by `for`/`id` (or wrapping), visible at all times. Placeholder text is never the only label.
2. **FE-242 — Instructions come before the field.** Format hints, constraints, and password rules appear before or within the label and are tied to the control with `aria-describedby`, where forms-mode screen readers encounter them — never revealed only after a failed submit.
3. **FE-243 — Validation fires on blur and submit, never earlier.** No error appears before the user's first blur or first submit attempt (inherited R-11.4-2). Keystroke-by-keystroke scolding is prohibited.
4. **FE-244 — Errors are inline, named, and summarized.** Each error sits next to its field, names the field and the fix in plain text, and is wired with `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby`. On submit, an error summary appears at the top and focus moves to it. One error per field at a time; never blame the user.
5. **FE-245 — Entered data survives errors.** A validation failure, a timeout, a reload, or back navigation never clears what the user typed (inherited R-11.4-1). The user fixes the one bad field, not the whole form.
6. **FE-246 — Use `autocomplete` for known data.** Name, email, address, payment, and one-time-code fields carry the standard `autocomplete` tokens so browsers and password managers can fill them.
7. **FE-247 — Required is marked in text.** Required fields say so in words ("required" in the label or legend), not by color or a bare asterisk alone; optional fields in a mostly-required form are marked "optional" instead.
8. **FE-248 — Submission is idempotent from the user's side.** The submit control disables on submit, retries reuse one idempotency key, and double-clicks cannot create duplicate records. Success ends in a confirmation (with ui-states), never silence.
9. **FE-249 — Multi-step flows stay short and honest.** 3–5 steps (target ≤3) with a progress indicator showing honest step counts; forms with legal, financial, or irreversible consequences include a review step before submission (inherited R-11.4-3). Multi-step forms save progress so the user can leave and resume.
10. **FE-250 — Signup stays minimal.** Signup targets ≤3 fields, hard maximum 5; any field beyond 3 needs a written justification in the project notes (inherited R-11.4-4).

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-121 — Placeholder as the only label.** Banned: an input whose placeholder is its sole label, disappearing the moment the user types. Defeats: DET-UX-022. Instead: a visible, associated label (FE-241); the placeholder may show an example format only. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-122 — Color-only error signals.** Banned: marking an error with only a red border or red text color, with no message. Defeats: DET-UX-021 (see also DET-UX-005). Instead: inline text naming the field and the fix, wired per FE-244. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-123 — Form wipes input on error.** Banned: clearing entered values when validation fails or the request errors. Defeats: DET-UX-007. Instead: preserve every value and flag only the bad field (FE-245). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-124 — Double-submit creates duplicates.** Banned: a submit path where a double-click, retry, or refresh-resubmit creates a second record or charge. Defeats: DET-UX-024. Instead: disable on submit plus a server-honored idempotency key (FE-248). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-125 — Submit that goes nowhere.** Banned: a form whose submit shows a success-looking state without a real request behind it. Defeats: DET-UX-003. Instead: a real endpoint, a real confirmation, and an error state when the request fails. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-FE-121 — axe-core form rules in CI.** Verifies: FE-241, FE-244, FE-247. Check: automated — run axe-core against every form page in CI and fail the build on label, `aria-invalid`, or describedby violations. Manual form (tool-form substitution): where no browser, axe-core runtime, or CI is available, perform the manual form inspection instead — verify every field has a persistent programmatic label, `aria-invalid` is set only on fields in error, and every error is tied to its field by `aria-describedby` — and record it in progress.md as a tool-form substitution for this gate; the automated axe-core run remains required wherever tooling exists. Pass: 0 violations (automated) or zero findings under the manual form. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-122 — Keyboard-only submit test.** Verifies: FE-243, FE-244, FE-245. Check: automated — Playwright, keyboard only: submit the empty form and assert focus lands on the error summary; correct all but one field, resubmit, and assert the remaining error names its field and every previously entered value is still present. Shape-adapted form: for a single-field form, the same assertions reduce to that field — submit it empty and assert focus lands on the error summary and the error names the field; enter an invalid value, resubmit, and assert the entered value is still present and the error still names the field; correct it and assert the submit succeeds. Pass: all assertions green. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-123 — Double-submit test.** Verifies: FE-248. Check: automated — Playwright double-clicks the submit control (and fires a duplicate request with the same idempotency key); assert exactly one record exists afterward. Pass: one record. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-124 — Screen-reader pass on the primary form.** Verifies: FE-242, FE-244, FE-247. Check: manual — complete the primary form with a screen reader in forms mode: every label, hint, and required marker is announced, and each error is reachable and understandable without sight. **Human-required:** this gate's evidence is a human listening to a real screen reader; no automated or agent-produced substitute satisfies it, and autonomous completion is blocked until the human pass is recorded. Agent-evidence form (interim evidence only — it prepares and de-risks the human pass but never replaces it): the agent records the G-FE-121 scan result, the G-FE-122 keyboard-test result, and an accessibility-tree audit of the form (every label, hint, required marker, and error association present in the tree) in progress.md, marks this gate human-required, and records a human-evidence waiver request naming the human pass still owed. Pass: the form is fully completable by ear, evidenced by the recorded human pass. Fail: warn, fix before release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Label first: visible, associated, never placeholder-only.
- Validate on blur and submit — never on the first keystroke.
- Errors name the field and the fix, inline and in a focused summary.
- Never lose the user's work.
- One submit, one record — no matter how many clicks.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every control has a visible associated label and hints before the field (FE-241, FE-242).
- [ ] axe-core form pass is clean in CI, or the manual form inspection is recorded as a tool-form substitution (G-FE-121).
- [ ] Keyboard-only submit test passes: focus on summary, errors name fields, data survives (G-FE-122).
- [ ] Double-submit test proves exactly one record (G-FE-123).
- [ ] Required fields are marked in text; autocomplete tokens are set (FE-246, FE-247).
- [ ] Screen-reader pass completed on the primary form (G-FE-124, human-required — agent-evidence form recorded until the human pass lands).
- [ ] Multi-step flows show honest progress and save/resume works (FE-249).

# frontend-core

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Core Web Vitals thresholds (web.dev, reproduced) — https://aemorph.com/guides/core-web-vitals/ ; Performance budgets in CI — https://www.debugutils.dev/blog/performance-budgets/
- **Depends on:** design-system, design-tokens
- **Feeds into:** component-library, layout-responsive, typography, ui-states

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building or reviewing any page or view — this is the base layer every other D3 skill assumes: semantic structure, the performance budget, the accessibility floor, and the rule that the frontend renders real data and real imagery only. WCPM §1 (priority & conflicts) and §9 (engineering) land here, as do the CC and CD cure families.
- **Do NOT use when:** the decision belongs to a specialist skill — token values to design-tokens, component internals to component-library, animation to motion. This skill sets the constraints those skills work inside; it does not replace them.

## Rules

1. **FE-001 — Semantic structure first.** Landmarks, headings, and native controls come before any component styling; framework components wrap native elements, and custom widgets are the last resort. (WCPM §1 priority order, R-1.x.)
2. **FE-002 — A clickable `div` is a defect.** Anything that responds to a click is a `<button>` or `<a>` with a real href, keyboard-operable and focusable. There is no styling exception.
3. **FE-003 — Reserved media dimensions.** Every image and video ships with `width`/`height` or an `aspect-ratio` so nothing shifts after load; layout stability is part of the CLS budget, not a polish step.
4. **FE-004 — Tokens only.** No hard-coded color, spacing, radius, or duration values in page or component code — semantic tokens from design-tokens are the only source (FE-041).
5. **FE-005 — The budget is a requirement.** Each route carries a JavaScript budget and the Core Web Vitals bars at the 75th percentile. A feature that breaks the budget is redesigned or split, never shipped heavy. Thresholds are cited from the numbers registry in `gates/`, per WCPM Appendix F — not restated here or per project.
6. **FE-006 — Real imagery only.** Imagery depicts the actual product, place, or people, or is clearly generic decoration. AI artifacts in photography (malformed hands, gibberish in-image text, warped logos) are a blocker, never a shrug (DET-VIS-024).
7. **FE-007 — Render real data only.** The frontend renders data that exists: no invented logos in "trusted by" rows, no unsourced stat bands, no placeholder avatars presented as people (WCPM Appendix A data/fabrication bans, D- working IDs). A claim the data cannot support is removed, not decorated.
8. **FE-008 — In-UI copy follows the copy rules.** Interface text carries no banned filler adjectives or verification phrases (WCPM Appendix A.4/A.5 word lists, CC cures); labels name the action or the thing, in the product's own vocabulary.
9. **FE-009 — The rendering surface serves search honestly.** Titles, meta descriptions, and structured data are rendered from the page's real content (WCPM §10 rendering surface; G-SCH family is designed to pass here, content owned by D9). Metadata describing content the page does not contain is a fabrication, not SEO.
10. **FE-010 — Works degraded before it works pretty.** Every page must function at 320px wide, on keyboard alone, and with images or scripts failed, before visual enhancement is layered on. Enhancement is progressive by construction.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-001 — AI artifacts in shipped photography.** Banned: publishing an image with malformed hands, gibberish in-image text, or warped logos. Defeats: DET-VIS-024. Instead: use real photography or a clearly illustrative graphic with no fake text or hands. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-002 — The clickable div.** Banned: `div`/`span` elements with click handlers standing in for buttons or links. Defeats: DET-VIS-032. Instead: a real `<button>` or `<a>` styled as the card's action. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-003 — The fake product mockup.** Banned: presenting a generic or blurred dashboard inside a browser/device frame as the product's UI. Defeats: DET-VIS-030. Instead: a current, readable screenshot of the actual product, framed plainly or not at all. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-004 — The invented logo cloud.** Banned: rendering customer or "featured in" logos that are invented, misspelled, or not the real marks. Defeats: DET-VIS-034. Instead: real customer logos with permission, correctly drawn — or no logo row. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-005 — The unsourced stat band.** Banned: rendering a band of round metrics with no source, date, or methodology behind them. Defeats: DET-VIS-035. Instead: specific, dated, sourced figures — or omit the band. Severity: WARN (escalates to a fabrication verdict under DET-CON-011 if no source exists).

## Gates

- **G-FE-001 — Performance budget in CI.** Verifies: FE-003, FE-005. Check: automated — Lighthouse CI assertions on key routes (`largest-contentful-paint` ≤ 2500ms, `cumulative-layout-shift` ≤ 0.1 as errors) plus a size-limit byte budget per route chunk. Local form (tool-form substitution): where Lighthouse CI is unavailable, run a local Lighthouse pass against the same routes and thresholds, or assert the byte budget locally with size-limit and record the metrics that cannot be measured locally as unmeasured rather than passed; record the substitution in progress.md, and the CI assertion remains required wherever CI exists. Pass: all assertions green (CI) or all locally assertable budgets green with unmeasured metrics recorded (local form). Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md. (Designed to pass the WCPM G-ENG engineering family.)
- **G-FE-002 — Accessibility floor scan.** Verifies: FE-001, FE-002, FE-010. Check: automated — axe-core run over key routes. Manual form (tool-form substitution): where no browser or axe-core runtime is available, perform the manual inspection instead — a keyboard-only traversal of the key routes at 320px with scripts disabled (FE-010), plus a source audit confirming landmarks and heading order (FE-001) and zero clickable `div`/`span` elements (FE-002) — and record it in progress.md as a tool-form substitution for this gate; the automated axe-core run remains required wherever tooling exists. Pass: zero critical violations (automated) or zero findings under the manual form. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-003 — Token-literal scan.** Verifies: FE-004. Check: automated — grep/stylelint pass over page and component style files for hex colors and raw px/ms literals outside the token source. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block until values move into tokens. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-004 — Imagery inspection.** Verifies: FE-006, FE-007. Check: manual — inspect every photographic image at 100% zoom for hands, in-image text, and logos; read every rendered logo and statistic aloud against its source. Pass: no artifacts, every mark real, every figure sourced. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Native elements first; a clickable div is a defect.
- The budget is a requirement, not a cleanup task.
- Render real data and real imagery, or render nothing.
- Works at 320px, keyboard-only, scripts failed — then pretty.
- Thresholds are cited from the registry, never restated.

## Checklist

- [ ] Landmarks, headings, and native controls carry the page structure (FE-001).
- [ ] No clickable divs or spans anywhere (G-FE-002, FE-002).
- [ ] Every image/video reserves its dimensions; CLS stays within budget (FE-003).
- [ ] Lighthouse CI and bundle budget are green for this route, or the local form is recorded as a tool-form substitution (G-FE-001).
- [ ] axe-core reports zero critical violations (G-FE-002).
- [ ] No raw color/spacing/duration literals outside tokens (G-FE-003).
- [ ] Every image inspected at 100%; no AI artifacts, no fake marks (G-FE-004).
- [ ] Every rendered statistic traces to a source with a date (FE-007).

# frontend-state

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Redux principles (single source of truth, read-only state, pure reducers), summarized at — https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/an-intro-to-redux-and-how-state-is-updated-in-a-redux-application-839c8334d1b1/ ; TanStack Query, Important Defaults (the server-state boundary) — https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults
- **Depends on:** frontend-core
- **Feeds into:** data-fetching, client-routing, pwa-offline

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** deciding where a piece of client-side state lives; introducing or refactoring a store; debugging views that disagree with each other; making view state shareable through the URL.
- **Do NOT use when:** the data comes from the server — fetching, caching, freshness, and refetch belong to data-fetching, and server data is never stored in this layer (FE-184). Do not use this skill to pick a state library's API details; it governs ownership and flow, not vendor syntax.

## Rules

1. **FE-181 — Classify before storing.** Every piece of state is classified before it is stored: local to one component, shared across the app (store), shareable view state (URL), or server data (not this layer — data-fetching).
2. **FE-182 — One owner, one update path.** Each shared fact has exactly one owner and one path by which it changes; two components holding copies of the same fact is a defect.
3. **FE-183 — No in-place mutation.** Shared state is never mutated directly from arbitrary components; changes go through the store's actions, reducers, or setters, so every change is traceable.
4. **FE-184 — Server data is never mirrored.** Server responses are never copied into the client store and hand-synchronized; the query cache (data-fetching) is their only home.
5. **FE-185 — The DOM is not a source of truth.** State is not stored in CSS classes, data attributes, or hidden inputs; the DOM renders state, it does not hold it.
6. **FE-186 — Shareable state lives in the URL.** Filters, selected tab, pagination, and sort order live in the URL, so refresh, the back button, and shared links land on the same view.
7. **FE-187 — Derived values are computed, not stored.** Anything calculable from stored state (totals, counts, filtered lists) is derived at read time, never kept as a second stored copy that can drift.
8. **FE-188 — Ownership is documented.** Each store slice records its owner fact, who may write it, and who reads it; an undocumented slice is treated as unowned and reviewed.
9. **FE-189 — Client flags are not session truth.** A client-side boolean (for example `isLoggedIn` in a store) never substitutes for the server's session and authorization checks; it may mirror them for display, and the server decides.
10. **FE-190 — Inherited state boundary.** The WCPM §9 engineering rules and the DAT parameter family's state/fetching boundary apply as cited in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md §2.2 and §2.4, and state work is designed to pass the G-ENG gate family.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-091 — Hand-synchronized server mirror.** Banned: copying server data into a global store and keeping it current with manual sync code. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Instead: read through the query cache and invalidate on mutation (data-fetching). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-092 — DOM as source of truth.** Banned: reading application state back from classes, data attributes, or hidden inputs. Defeats: DET-FAKE-016. Instead: state lives in the store; the DOM only renders it (FE-185). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-093 — Client flag as authorization truth.** Banned: gating data or actions on a client-side flag instead of the server's session check. Defeats: DET-FAKE-002. Instead: the API authorizes every request; the flag only shapes display (FE-189). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-094 — The same fact stored twice.** Banned: keeping one fact in two places (store plus component state, or two slices) with independent updates. Defeats: DET-FAKE-005. Instead: one owner (FE-182); every other view derives or subscribes. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-091 — Trace test.** Verifies: FE-182, FE-187. Check: manual — for each shared fact, name its owner and update path from the slice documentation, change it in one view, and confirm every dependent view updates without a reload. Pass: every fact traces and propagates. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-092 — Mutation lint.** Verifies: FE-183. Check: automated where the stack provides one — run the store's immutability lint (for example a Redux-style rule forbidding direct state mutation outside reducers). Pass: zero violations. Fail: block shipment. If the stack has no such rule, its absence is recorded in progress.md and G-FE-091 carries the weight. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-093 — URL state round-trip.** Verifies: FE-186. Check: automated — Playwright sets filters, tab, and page; reloads; opens the same URL in a fresh page. Pass: both pages render the identical view state. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-094 — Store mirror scan.** Verifies: FE-184. Check: automated — grep the store slices for assignments of API response payloads (response types, `fetch`/`axios` results written into reducers). Pass: no hand-mirrored server data in the store. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Classify before you store: local, shared, URL, server.
- One fact, one owner, one update path.
- Server data is never mirrored by hand.
- The DOM renders state; it never holds it.
- If it can be computed, do not store it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every shared fact has a named owner and update path (FE-182, FE-188).
- [ ] Trace test passes for all shared facts (G-FE-091).
- [ ] No server payloads are stored in client slices (G-FE-094).
- [ ] Filters, tab, and pagination survive reload and link sharing (G-FE-093).
- [ ] No state is read back from the DOM (FE-185).
- [ ] No client flag substitutes for a server session check (FE-189).
- [ ] Mutation lint is clean, or its absence is recorded (G-FE-092).

# layout-responsive

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D3 Frontend, Design & Motion (FE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** GOV.UK Design System, layout styles — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/layout/ ; WCAG 2.2 criteria summary (reflow SC 1.4.10, target size SC 2.5.8) — https://convarso.com/blog/web-accessibility-guide-wcag/
- **Depends on:** design-tokens, design-system
- **Feeds into:** frontend-core, forms, data-visualisation

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building or reviewing any page or component layout; choosing breakpoints or container widths; fixing overflow, clipping, or a mobile view that is a squeezed desktop page.
- **Do NOT use when:** the decision is a token value (spacing, radius scales) — that is design-tokens. Do not use this skill to justify hiding content on mobile; hiding is a content decision owned by the page's requirements, and FE-131 still applies.

## Rules

1. **FE-121 — No page-level horizontal scrolling.** At every width from 320 CSS px up, the page itself never scrolls horizontally (DET-VIS-038; WCAG 1.4.10 reflow). Overflow is fixed in the layout, never by clipping the page.
2. **FE-122 — Breakpoints where content breaks.** Layouts are fluid first; a breakpoint is added at the width where the content actually fails, and breakpoints are named for the layout change (`nav-collapses`, `cards-two-up`), never for a device.
3. **FE-123 — Mobile is recomposed, not stacked.** Small-screen layouts reorder by priority — primary content and actions first — instead of stacking desktop DOM order top to bottom (DET-VIS-037).
4. **FE-124 — Targets stay tappable at every width.** Interactive targets are at least 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 floor) at every breakpoint; 44px is the working target for primary actions.
5. **FE-125 — Heroes size to content.** Hero height comes from `min-height` plus content and padding; fixed `100vh` or pixel heights that can clip text or CTAs on short screens are forbidden (DET-VIS-039).
6. **FE-126 — Width follows content role.** Reading content, galleries, data tables, and media each get the width their role needs; one container width applied to every section is a defect (DET-VIS-005).
7. **FE-127 — Reading measure is held.** Body-text columns stay near 45–80 characters at wide viewports instead of running to the container edge.
8. **FE-128 — Media space is reserved before load.** Every image and embed carries `width`/`height` or an `aspect-ratio`, so layout does not shift when assets arrive (CLS budget, frontend-core).
9. **FE-129 — Components respond to their own space.** A component used in both wide and narrow contexts adapts with container queries to the space it is given, not with page-level breakpoints written for one placement.
10. **FE-130 — Wide content is contained or reformatted.** Tables, code blocks, and charts get a contained scroll region or a small-screen reformat (stacked rows, priority columns); they never force page overflow and are never silently truncated.
11. **FE-131 — Nothing essential disappears on small screens.** Content or actions removed at a breakpoint must be reachable another way on that viewport; "it didn't fit" is not a removal reason (DET-VIS-037).
12. **FE-132 — Inherited layout law.** The WCPM LAY, SEC, and SPC parameter families apply as cited in docs/WCPM_MAPPING.md §2.4, and layout work is designed to pass the G-EXP gate family.

## BAN list

- **BAN-FE-061 — Fixed-height hero.** Banned: a hero with a fixed `100vh` or pixel height whose text or CTA clips on short or landscape screens. Defeats: DET-VIS-039. Instead: `min-height` sized by content, with the CTA always in flow. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-062 — Page-level horizontal overflow.** Banned: shipping a page where `scrollWidth` exceeds the viewport at any width ≥ 320px. Defeats: DET-VIS-038. Instead: a contained scroll region or a stacked reformat for the table (FE-130). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-063 — Essential content hidden on mobile.** Banned: `display: none` on content or actions at small breakpoints with no alternate path to them. Defeats: DET-VIS-037. Instead: recompose by priority (FE-123) or move the content behind a reachable disclosure. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-FE-064 — One container width for every section.** Banned: a single `.container` max-width governing prose, galleries, tables, and media alike. Defeats: DET-VIS-005. Instead: width tokens per content role (FE-126). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-FE-065 — Uniform section template.** Banned: every section shipping with identical padding, alignment, and loudest element regardless of its role. Defeats: DET-VIS-001. Instead: composition varies by section role, per design-system. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-FE-061 — Overflow assertion.** Verifies: FE-121, FE-130. Check: automated — Playwright loads every route at 320/390/768/1440px and asserts `document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth` on each. Pass: zero routes overflow at any width. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-062 — Screenshot matrix review.** Verifies: FE-123, FE-125, FE-131. Check: manual — review screenshots at 320/390/768/1440px per main page; confirm priority order on mobile, unclipped heroes, and no essential content missing at small widths. Pass: all four widths conform. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-063 — Target-size audit.** Verifies: FE-124. Check: automated — a script reads computed sizes of all interactive elements at 390px and fails any below 24×24 CSS px. Pass: zero undersized targets. Fail: warn; a primary action below the floor blocks. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-FE-064 — Resize walk.** Verifies: FE-122, FE-127. Check: manual — drag the viewport continuously from 320px to 1920px on the main pages, watching for overlap, orphaned controls, and unreadable line lengths between breakpoints. Pass: no failure at any intermediate width. Fail: warn and log the failing width range. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No page scroll sideways, ever, from 320px up.
- Mobile is recomposed by priority, not stacked.
- Heroes size to content; nothing essential is hidden.
- Width follows the content's role.
- Breakpoints live where content breaks, not on devices.

## Checklist

- [ ] Overflow assertion passes on every route at 320/390/768/1440px (G-FE-061).
- [ ] Mobile order follows priority, not desktop DOM order (FE-123).
- [ ] All interactive targets are ≥ 24×24 CSS px at mobile widths (G-FE-063).
- [ ] Heroes use `min-height` and cannot clip text or CTAs (FE-125).
- [ ] Container widths vary by content role (FE-126).
- [ ] Wide tables and code are contained or reformatted (FE-130).
- [ ] Nothing essential is unreachable on small screens (FE-131).
